title: Precision Patcher: severity-driven emergency patching, branching and backport model
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Problem: We lack a predictable, low-friction emergency patch flow that maps severity to branching, automated backports, and rollout gating. Current ad-hoc hotpatches have caused mis-scoped backports, unclear owner handoffs, and missed canary windows during high-severity incidents.

Goal: Define a deterministic 'Precision Patcher' process: a severity taxonomy, explicit emergency branch naming, automated backport jobs, sign-off gates for canary/gradual rollouts, and a lightweight escalation playbook for triage leads. The outcome should reduce time-to-safe-patch, minimize human error during backports, and provide an audit trail for compliance.

Proposal summary:
1) Severity bands: S0 - catastrophic (data loss/PII leak/high availability outage), S1 - production outage (major feature degradation), S2 - functional regression with limited scope, S3 - cosmetic/low-risk. Each band maps to required approvals, target SLA for mitigation, and backport depth (e.g., backport to latest LTS + 1 previous for S0/S1).
2) Emergency branch naming: emergency/{major}.{minor}/{YYYYMMDD}/{ENG-key}/{short-desc} (example: emergency/2.4/20260310/ENG-21834/faster-kv-evict). Branches are created from the active LTS branch for the affected release.
3) Patch-train and backport policy: For S0/S1 the default is patch to the currently deployed LTS and the prior LTS if still supported; for S2 only the current LTS; S3 handled as normal release cycle. Backports must be implemented as cherry-picks with signed commits and include an automated backport CI job (backport-ci) that validates compile, integration tests, and a minimal e2e smoke using a small dataset.
4) Rollout gates: a checklist gating system integrated into the release-runner: build green, security sign-off (if PII/crypto), QA quick-sign, canary window (configurable; default 30m with progressive traffic ramp), automatic rollback threshold based on error rate and latency deltas. All gating decisions recorded in the ticket timeline and tagged to the release artifact.
5) Automation and tooling: implement two pipeline primitives: 1) emergency-branch-creator (creates branch + labels + backport job matrix), 2) emergency-release-runner (creates canary release, watches metrics, triggers rollback when thresholds exceeded). Add a backport dashboard in Console showing pending backports and conflicts.
6) Communication & audit: require a short incident-annotation on the ticket describing customer exposure, timeline of fix, and list of backported branches; artifacts must include PR links, signed commits, and CI run IDs.

Constraints and trade-offs:
- Broad backporting reduces blast radius but increases release surface and review overhead. We limit backports for S1/S0 only to LTS lines still receiving security fixes.
- Automated backports will occasionally produce conflicts; conflict resolution is manual with triage owner assignment. We'll surface conflicts early via CI and assign a 1-hour SLA for triage owner to acknowledge.
- Canary windows add delay to mean time to mitigation for S0 but are required when rollback can cause more harm than a mitigated patch. For S0 where immediate rollback is unacceptable, we allow an emergency-accelerated gate with async approvals from on-call SRE + Release Eng lead.

Deliverables: documented severity matrix, emergency branch template, a GitHub Actions backport workflow, release-runner gating config, console backport dashboard prototype, runbook section for triage and sign-offs.
acceptance_criteria: Written severity matrix committed to release-infra docs and linked in the runbook
Emergency branch naming and creation script (emergency-branch-creator) that creates branch + initial PR template
backport-ci workflow that runs for each cherry-pick and fails fast on conflicts, posting diagnostics to the ticket
release-runner gate implementation with configurable canary windows and automated rollback thresholds
Console backport dashboard showing active emergency branches, backport status, and conflict flags
At least one staged S1 patch exercised end-to-end in staging using new flow (dry-run) and retro documented
